Evaluate whether schedule disadvantages show up in outcomes

Source: R/eval_rest_impact.R
eval_rest_impact.Rd

Joins the composite schedule advantage to game results and, optionally, injury reports, then compares disadvantaged and advantaged teams. The output is descriptive: win rates, spread cover rates, scoring margins, and injury counts for games where one team had an edge. It does not estimate a causal effect of rest or travel.

Usage

eval_rest_impact(
  schedule,
  outcomes = NULL,
  injuries = NULL,
  advantage = NULL,
  metrics = c("rest", "travel", "time_zone", "composite"),
  injury_statuses = c("Out", "Doubtful"),
  min_edge = 0,
  ...
)

Arguments

schedule

A schedule accepted by calculate_schedule_advantage().

outcomes

Optional data frame with game_id, home_score, and away_score (and optionally spread_line). Use this when the schedule does not already carry results. Columns in outcomes override matching columns in schedule.

injuries

Optional injury report with season, week, team, and a report_status or status column, such as the output of nflreadr::load_injuries(). When NULL, injury columns are NA.

advantage

Optional precomputed output from calculate_schedule_advantage(). When NULL, it is computed from schedule (and ...).

metrics

Which components to evaluate: any of "rest", "travel", "time_zone", and "composite". Defaults to all four.

injury_statuses

Injury statuses counted as unavailable. Defaults to c("Out", "Doubtful").

min_edge

Minimum absolute edge required to count a game as disadvantaged. Defaults to 0, which includes any non-zero edge. The units follow the selected metric (rest days, miles, body-clock hours, or composite points); use something like 0.5 for the composite.

...

Arguments passed to calculate_schedule_advantage() when advantage is NULL.

Value

A tibble with one row per metric. games is the number of games with a non-missing component; disadvantaged_games counts games at or above min_edge. Win rates exclude ties from their denominators, and cover rates exclude pushes. Injury summaries cover games with injury data for both teams.

Details

A positive component favors the home team, so the away team is the disadvantaged side; a negative component makes the home team disadvantaged. Games with abs(edge) < min_edge are left out of the disadvantaged/advantaged comparison. win_rate_diff, cover_rate_diff, and injury_diff are always disadvantaged minus advantaged, so a negative value means the disadvantaged side did worse.

Examples

advantage <- calculate_schedule_advantage(nfl_schedules_sample)
eval_rest_impact(nfl_schedules_sample, advantage = advantage)
#> # A tibble: 4 x 18
#>   metric    games disadvantaged_games disadvantaged_win_games disadvantaged_wins
#>   <chr>     <int>               <int>                   <int>              <int>
#> 1 rest        538                 219                     219                109
#> 2 travel      570                 570                     569                267
#> 3 time_zone   570                 336                     336                160
#> 4 composite   570                 570                     569                262
#> # i 13 more variables: disadvantaged_win_rate <dbl>, advantaged_win_rate <dbl>,
#> #   win_rate_diff <dbl>, mean_margin_disadvantaged <dbl>, cover_games <int>,
#> #   disadvantaged_covers <int>, disadvantaged_cover_rate <dbl>,
#> #   advantaged_cover_rate <dbl>, cover_rate_diff <dbl>, injury_games <int>,
#> #   mean_injuries_disadvantaged <dbl>, mean_injuries_advantaged <dbl>,
#> #   injury_diff <dbl>
